labels.label: blem:suspendre

hypotheses.paper: quotient of an open Omega of M^n by isometries acting freely and properly discontinuously (l.1837-1838)
Gamma preserves a timelike affine subspace U (l.1839)
hypotheses.note: added RestrictsIn iota Gamma (each element restricts to U as an SO0-affine isometry, i.e. preserves the orientation of U); implies preservation (RestrictsIn.preserves); necessary for every parametrization of U (not_restrictsIn_glideGroup_of_range). U = range iota with iota orthochronous (hι : iota.Orthochronous, Barbot's time-oriented convention l.469-480); no loss: exists_affineMinkEmbedding_of_isTimelike now returns an orthochronous iota (f chosen future). Spatial orientation of iota not asked (not canonical: depends on an orientation of U^perp).

hypotheses.paper: Omega invariant by translations by U^perp (l.1840-1841)
hypotheses.note: forall w in iota.perp, forall p in Omega, p + w in Omega; equivalent to Omega + w = Omega (perpInvariant_iff). This is BARBOT-THEOREMS §6 G6, carried as a hypothesis; its proof for Omega(S~) is owed downstream.

findings: Lemma 5.5 (l.1836-1844) is false as written in dimension >= 3: in M^3 the glide gamma(t,x) = (t+1,-x) is in Isom(M^3) (linear part diag(1,-1,-1), det 1), generates a free properly discontinuous Z on Omega = M^3 (invariant under all translations), preserves the timelike plane U = {x_2 = 0}, but restricts to U as (t,x) -> (t+1,-x), det -1, not in Isom(M^2) = SO0-affine (Barbot's convention l.469-480); Gamma\U is a non-orientable timelike Moebius strip, not a flat spacetime in Barbot's sense. Fix: ask that Gamma preserve the orientation of U (true after passing to a subgroup of index <= 2, consistent with Theorem A's 'up to finite coverings'). Formalized as TwistedProduct.not_restrictsIn_glideGroup (for iota = plane) and, independently of the parametrization, TwistedProduct.not_restrictsIn_glideGroup_of_range (every iota' with range = {x_2 = 0}: the restriction is linearly conjugate to the flip, det -1); the corrected lemma is suspendre (DEC-27).
notes: 'the linear twisted product of M by U^perp' (l.1843-1844) is read in the quotient form of BARBOT-THEOREMS §1 (IsLTPOver: B = Gamma\Omega, M = Gamma_U\(U cap Omega)), adopted with DEC-43; the suspension structure of §5.S is proved at the level of Omega (split, split_smul: gamma acts on M^{d1+1} x U^perp diagonally by (g, L(gamma)|U^perp), a linear isometry of the euclidean U^perp) and not descended to a bundle map B -> M.
Omega is not asked to be connected (not a paper hypothesis): M is connected because B is (connectedSpace_base).

labels.label: produi
notes: Definition in BARBOT-THEOREMS §1 quotient form (DEC-43 reading R1), not §5.S's suspension of M~ x N by pi_1(M). IsLTPData carries, beside BARBOT-THEOREMS §1: `orthochronous` (iota preserves time orientation; without it iota = (t,x) -> (-t,x), Gamma = 1, Omega = {t>0} gives IsLTPOver {t>0} {t<0}, the time reverse, not isometric as a time-oriented flat spacetime — audit blocking finding, fixed) and `restricts` (RestrictsIn, needed to define Gamma restricted to U as a subgroup of Isom(M^{d1+1}) — see the blem:suspendre finding). Fields `timelike` and `preserves` are derivable (timelikeImage, RestrictsIn.preserves) and kept to mirror BARBOT-THEOREMS §1. Non-vacuity: trivial LTP (iota = id, every quotient over itself), the product M^n over the time axis (Gamma = 1), and Z e0\M^n over the timelike circle Z\M^1 (Gamma != 1); all with orthochronous iota.

labels.label: rem:5.3 (causal half, l.1800-1805)

sorries.obstruction: the causal structure of a quotient Gamma\Omega is not available (Flat.Quotient SCOPE: lifting <= on the top open set through chains of local relations is not proved), and comparing <=_Omega with <=_{U cap Omega} along the retraction needs reparametrizing the image of a causal curve as a graph over the time of M^{d1+1}, plus a fibre bound for compactness of diamonds; Barbot's own argument (t o q a proper time function) goes through Geroch (iii)=>(i), itself a cited sorry in GerochEquiv. Only the linear core (retract is a causal map of M^n onto M^{d1+1} for orthochronous iota) is proved.

notes: Only the linear-twisted-product case of Rem 5.3 is stated; the remark (l.1801-1805) covers twisted products by every euclidean manifold, flat tori included. Orthochronous iota is now part of IsLTPData, so the proved linear core (retract_le_top) applies to every IsLTPOver.

labels.label: rem:5.4 (l.1816-1828)
notes: Rem 5.4 concerns Bieberbach / finite index, not causality; out of this package's scope.

kb_proposals: An SO0(1,d) element preserving a timelike affine subspace U restricts to U only in O+(1,d1): any (Isom,M^n)-structure statement about Gamma\U needs an orientation hypothesis on U (RestrictsIn).

Sylvester for a timelike subspace: LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_orthogonal_basis on minkB restricted to f^perp cap D (f unit timelike) gives the isometric parametrization; see exists_affineMinkEmbedding_of_isTimelike.
In a proof, `set n := Module.finrank ℝ W` after obtaining a basis `b : Basis (Fin (finrank ℝ W))` shadows b and makes hypotheses about it refer to b✝; write finrank out instead.

A definition 'X is a twisted product over Y' through an isometric embedding iota must ask iota orthochronous in a time-oriented setting; otherwise it relates X to the time reverse of Y (audit of WP-31d).
